questions.prompt: Did your loved one own a home?
Was there a mortgage on the home?
Did they have a life insurance policy?
Do you have a will on file?
Do you have a life insurance policy?

checklistItems.title: Notify the mortgage lender
checklistItems.description: Let the lender know the borrower has died so payments and account access are handled correctly.

checklistItems.title: Decide whether to sell, rent, or keep the property
checklistItems.description: An inherited home often needs a decision fairly quickly. A realtor experienced with estate sales can help you weigh the options.

checklistItems.title: File a life insurance claim
checklistItems.description: Contact the insurer with a certified copy of the death certificate to start the claims process.

gaps.title: No will on file
gaps.description: Without a will, state law decides how your estate is divided and who cares for any minor children. A probate or estate lawyer can help you put one in place.

gaps.title: No life insurance policy
gaps.description: Life insurance gives your family a financial cushion. A financial advisor can help you find a policy that fits your situation.

articles.title: What to do in the first 48 hours after a death
articles.body: The first two days are about the essentials: get a legal pronouncement of death, arrange transportation of the body, and notify close family. Everything else on the checklist can wait a few days.
